title: Aius carrier - optical-spdif sheet
description: Reset-safe optical S/PDIF path: Cliff ORJ5 TOSLINK receiver -> bypass mux
(SN74LVC1G3157) -> TX gate (SN74LVC1G126) -> Cliff OTJ5 TOSLINK transmitter.
The receiver drives the global SPDIF_RX (terminated at Teensy pin 15) and also
feeds the mux raw-bypass input. The mux selects the transmit source between the
Teensy processed output (SPDIF_TX, pin 14) and the raw ORJ5 bypass; the gate
holds the transmitter idle until firmware enables it. All logic runs at 3.3 V.

design_notes.mux_truth_table: SN74LVC1G3157 SPDT analog switch: select pin S (pin 6) = PATH_SELECT. S LOW -> common A (pin 4) = B1 (pin 3); S HIGH -> A = B2 (pin 1). B1 is wired to the PROCESSED source (SPDIF_TX, Teensy pin 14) and B2 to the RAW bypass (SPDIF_RX, the ORJ5 output). PATH_SELECT has a 10k pull-down on the teensy-expansion sheet (R17), so the hardware default is S LOW = processed path, exactly the interfaces-and-states spdif-path-select reset default. HIGH selects the diagnostic raw bypass.
design_notes.tx_gate_oe_polarity: SAFETY-CRITICAL. The gate is an SN74LVC1G126, whose output-enable is ACTIVE-HIGH (OE on pin 1): OE LOW -> output Y (pin 4) high-impedance; OE HIGH -> Y = A. TX_ENABLE is active-HIGH with a 10k pull-down (R18) on the teensy-expansion sheet, so its reset/absent default is LOW. OE is therefore driven DIRECTLY by TX_ENABLE: at reset TX_ENABLE LOW -> OE LOW -> Y high-Z -> transmitter idle, with no inverter and no fail-safe pull-up needed. (This replaced an earlier 1G125 active-low-OE gate that required an added inverter + pull-up; the 1G126 is the correct single-part solution.)
design_notes.tx_idle_level: When the gate output is high-impedance (TX disabled), R40 (10k) pulls the gate output / OTJ5 Vin (TX_GATED) to GND, giving the transmitter a defined idle logic level (no optical carrier) instead of a floating input. OTJ5 Vin min VIH is 2.0 V, so the pulled-low idle is unambiguously a logic low.
design_notes.reset_safe_summary: With the Teensy absent, held in reset, booting, or crashed, the two teensy-side pull-downs alone establish the safe optical state before firmware runs: R17 (PATH_SELECT low) selects the processed path at the mux, and R18 (TX_ENABLE low) -> gate OE low holds the TX gate high-Z, so the OTJ5 sees the R40-defined idle and emits no data. Path selection is only ever changed by firmware while TX is muted (interfaces-and-states raw-bypass-request).
design_notes.levels: 3.3 V logic throughout. ORJ5 output min VOH 2.4 V drives the mux/Teensy CMOS inputs; the >=16 Mbit/s S/PDIF bandwidth is met by the LVC logic (typ. 340 MHz analog switch, 3.7 ns gate) and the 16 Mbit/s ORJ5/OTJ5 modules.
design_notes.decoupling: Per Cliff datasheets: C20 (100nF) decouples ORJ5 Vcc within 7 mm; C21 (30pF) sits GND-to-Vout on the ORJ5 to avoid the loading effect; C25 (100nF) decouples OTJ5 Vcc. C22/C24 (100nF) decouple the mux and gate +3V3 pins.
design_notes.bom_change: The tx-gate part changes from SN74LVC1G125 (active-low OE) to SN74LVC1G126 (active-high OE) so TX_ENABLE drives OE directly with no inverter. provisional-components.csv / aius-hardware-spec spdif-tx-gate must be updated to the 1G126; no inverter part is added.

components.desc: TOSLINK optical S/PDIF receiver: optical in -> SPDIF_RX + raw-bypass mux input
S/PDIF bypass mux (SPDT): B1=processed (SPDIF_TX), B2=raw (SPDIF_RX), S=PATH_SELECT
optical TX gate: A=MUX_OUT, OE=TX_ENABLE (active high), Y=TX_GATED (high-Z when disabled)
TOSLINK optical S/PDIF transmitter: gated logic in -> optical out
ORJ5 Vcc decoupling (0.1uF within 7 mm per datasheet)
ORJ5 GND-to-Vout loading cap (30pF per datasheet precaution)
OTJ5 Vcc decoupling (0.1uF within 7 mm per datasheet)
TX_GATED / OTJ5 Vin pull-down: defined idle low when the gate is high-Z
